reaction.episode: CORRECTION episode through the Nov 18 close: SPX 7,323.63, down 6.64% from its 120-day high, 4.25% below its 50-day and 0.31% below its 200-day; SMH $459.54 and NVDA $150.96 both below Zone 2; VIX 24.56 at the close (26.78 midday, +9.04%) and HY OAS 3.47 calm, with the mechanical capitulation tally at 1 of 4.
reaction.invalidation: SPX closes back above its 50-day (7,648.51) with SMH reclaiming Zone 2 and VIX under 25 — the correction call is wrong, the stance moves to Probe/Add and the ladder is void.

ladder.response: Escalation to the next zone down: stay Watch, no new adds; Tranche A stays un-armed and cash stays in bills.
ladder.trigger: SPX closes below 7,300 or SMH closes below $450

ladder.response: Treat as a bull trap: do not chase the first bounce; any Probe entries wait for the failure-zone retest verdict, and trim into strength on rejection.
ladder.trigger: Bounce into the failure zone (SPX 7,750-7,820 or SMH 580-600) that fails and rolls over

ladder.response: Full stand-down / regime break: no Probe under any zone print until credit calms and VIX rolls back under 25.
ladder.trigger: VIX closes above 25 while HY OAS pushes above 4%

ladder.response: Re-entry condition met: move to Probe per the deployment ladder (Tranche A, 25%) — zone print plus tally, not price alone.
ladder.trigger: SMH or NVDA reclaims Zone 2 (SMH $470-505, NVDA $175-185) with the mechanical tally at 3 of 4 or better

reaction.trapRisk: The pivot-and-fail scenario is the base risk here: NVDA at RSI 20.3 and a 6.64% SPX drawdown invite dip-buying, but with zone occupancy, volume climax, and VIX rollover all unconfirmed, the first bounce is more likely to fail into the 7,750-7,820 failure zone than to hold. Entries wait for the failed first bounce plus a second low that holds; no chasing intraday green, no sizing on oversold alone.

strategyPosture: Watch. The correction is confirmed and deepening — SPX below its 200-day, SMH and NVDA below Zone 2, VIX above 25 — but no capitulation signal has confirmed (tally 1 of 4), so there is nothing to add into yet; hold cash and let the tape prove a bottom.

themes.counterRead: The divergence is real and worth tracking, but nothing in the credit data confirms a broad rollover yet. If lending standards tighten or HY OAS pushes above 4%, the rotation read dies and the rollover read takes over. Until then, index-level calm is masking concentrated pain, not hiding a systemic break.
themes.dataAnchor: Mag7 names average 20.21% below their 52-week highs against SPY only 7.9% below its high — a 12.31-point divergence gap — while bank lending standards are LOOSE (SLOOS 1.7%, far below the ~40% stress threshold) and HY OAS sits at 3.47, calm. SPY itself is down 6.77% in a month, not in freefall. The weakness is concentrated in the index's heaviest names, not in credit.
themes.label: Mag7 rotation, not rollover
themes.narrative: The market reads the AI-leader selloff as the start of a broad rollover: NVDA is 39.1% off its high and QQQ is down 10.35% in a month.
themes.watchFor: HY OAS above 4% or SLOOS moving toward the 40% stress zone would void the rotation read.

themes.counterRead: Revenue growth does not set a floor by itself: NVDA at $148.20 is below its $175-185 Zone 2 and SMH at $459.54 is below its $470-505 Zone 2, with no volume climax or VIX rollover confirmed. The opportunity is real but early — the data says the businesses are building, the tape says nobody is paying for it yet, and buying into a falling tape without a zone reclaim is catching, not investing.
themes.dataAnchor: NVDA revenue is growing 61.4% YoY while the stock sits 39.1% below its high at RSI 20.3. The same gap repeats across the complex: AVGO revenue +55% YoY, 29.7% off its high; DDOG +27.7% YoY, 44.1% off its high; ONTO +41.5% YoY, 48.8% off its high; MDB +22.8% YoY, 36.5% off its high. Insiders bought at the trough in KTOS ($0.2M), ETN ($0.17M) and VST ($1.17M). SMH is 31.6% off its high and down 17.45% in 20 days — a sentiment drawdown, not an earnings one.
themes.label: AI fundamentals ahead of price
themes.narrative: The AI trade is broken: circular financing, a leadership vacuum at NVDA, and capex-cut headlines have the market pricing the AI buildout as a bust.
themes.watchFor: SMH or NVDA closing back inside Zone 2 (SMH $470-505, NVDA $175-185) with the mechanical tally at 3 of 4 or better.

themes.counterRead: The one clean leg is credit: HY OAS 3.47 with no cracking. Corrections that end without a credit event tend to bottom on a failed first bounce plus a second low that holds, not on a single washout day. Nothing in the tape has printed that structure yet, so the honest read is 'still falling, no bottom signal' — not 'oversold, must bounce'.
themes.dataAnchor: SPX closed Nov 18 at 7,323.63, down 6.64% from its 120-day high, 4.25% below its 50-day (7,648.51) and 0.31% below its 200-day (7,346.55). SMH and NVDA are both BELOW_ZONE_2. VIX closed 24.56 on Nov 18 with a 5-day high of 25.46 and sits at 26.78 midday — above the 25 stand-down line. The mechanical capitulation tally is 1 of 4: only credit calm is confirmed; zone occupancy, volume climax reversal, and VIX rollover are all unconfirmed.
themes.label: Correction deepening, no capitulation yet
themes.narrative: The tape is weak and getting weaker: SPY down 1.3% on the day, QQQ down 1.42%, VIX up 9.04% to 26.78.
themes.watchFor: A failed first bounce followed by a second low that holds above the Nov 18 close, with VIX rolling over from its 5-day high of 25.46.

themes.counterRead: Expensive money explains the multiple compression in growth names, but it does not explain a credit break that has not happened. The rate story and the credit story agree: tight financial conditions, no funding crisis. The Dec hike question matters for the next leg of rates, not for whether the system is breaking.
themes.dataAnchor: The 10-year sits at 5.10% with the 2-year at 4.80% and the curve steepening to +0.30 on 2s10s; the real 10-year is 2.91% and the Fed funds rate is 3.88%. The FOMC minutes (Oct 27-28) are the active high-signal event, with the Dec 8-9 FOMC decision and Dec 10 CPI next. Against that, credit is not stressed: HY OAS 3.47, lending standards LOOSE at 1.7%.
themes.label: Rates high, credit calm
themes.narrative: Money is expensive and the Fed is the problem: the 10-year at 5.1% is strangling growth multiples, and the Dec 8-9 FOMC decision looms over every bid.
themes.watchFor: Dec 8-9 FOMC outcome and Dec 10 CPI; a 10-year sustained above 5.5% or HY OAS above 4% changes the read.

themes.counterRead: Nothing here is a new thesis failure; it is the known cost of holding leveraged exposure through a 6.64% index drawdown. The risk is behavioral, not analytical: the sleeves will keep amplifying every down day until the index stabilizes, so sizing — not re-underwriting — is the decision.
themes.dataAnchor: TQQQ is down 30.86% in a month and 4.26% today, against QQQ down 10.35% in a month — almost exactly the mechanical 3x of the index move, not a separate break. CONL is down 62.95% in a month and BMNR 35.81%, while IAU is down 11.05% and VST 20.21%. The drawdown concentrates exactly where leverage and beta live, which is what leverage does in a correction.
themes.label: Leveraged sleeves absorb the drawdown
themes.narrative: The portfolio's speculative sleeves are collapsing: TQQQ and CONL look like thesis breaks.
themes.watchFor: QQQ stabilizing (a close back above its 50-day) is the signal the leveraged sleeves stop amplifying the downside.

VIX daily close below 25 after a 5-day high of 25.46
SPX close back above its 200-day (7,346.55), then its 50-day (7,648.51)
HY OAS holding below 4% (now 3.47) versus cracking above 4%
Dec 8-9 FOMC decision and Dec 10 CPI prints
whereWaveBuilds: The next move builds in the AI complex: NVDA at RSI 20.3 with revenue growing 61.4% YoY and SMH 31.6% off its high — the first reclaim of Zone 2 (SMH $470-505) with a VIX rollover is the trigger that turns this from a falling tape into a Probe.
